source.expected_dataset_subject: Four nettle-feeding butterfly species, 19 Swedish sites, two years 2017–2018, 6,777 collected larvae

scientific_question: Can detailed empirical butterfly–parasitoid outcomes calibrate the distinction between coarse host-linked opportunity and realized enemy-linked demographic quality, without repeating the 2021 paper?
published_prior_art: The paper already tested butterfly assemblage presence, larval abundance, within-season phenology, latitudinal gradients, time since Araschnia levana establishment and parasitoid-sharing effects
A separate 2020 study already analysed parasitoid-host phenological overlap, including Phobocampe confusa
This is a native nettle (Urtica dioica) system with butterfly range expansion, NOT host-plant introduction, so it cannot test anthropogenic botanical redistribution.

required: file identifiers and checksums, source license
open raw batch monitoring tables with egg/larval sample size, death causes, named parasitoids, site, date and butterfly species
genuine observation denominators and consistent units
source_gate.if_source_available: inventory schema and quality only; do not fit outcomes until any distinct estimand is frozen and mapped against 2021 article and all coanalyses

biological_scope.unknown_introduced_botanical_status: The focal Urtica dioica is the resident nettle host in the Swedish study; no experimental exotic-host factor
not_observed: butterfly populations on novel introduced host plants
host plant species variation within sites
independent recruitment through mating and fecundity

novelty_gate: No claim of new butterfly parasitoid indirect-interaction discovery from refitting existing 2021 model. A new prediction requires an independently specified heldout-site/year test not already published, robust to climate/site confounding, and explicit labeling as a secondary published-data analysis; population fitness or botanical invasion remains unidentifiable.
